quiz.q: How did the structural design of SAPTA differ fundamentally from SAFTA in approaching regional trade barriers?
options: SAPTA used a restrictive positive list, whereas SAFTA adopted an ambitious negative list covering unlisted goods.
SAPTA eliminated tariffs on all consumer goods, whereas SAFTA restricted concessions solely to agricultural commodities.
SAPTA mandated uniform tariff cuts for all states, whereas SAFTA excluded least developed countries from concessions.
SAPTA established a binding dispute settlement body, whereas SAFTA relied entirely on voluntary bilateral negotiations.
quiz.why: SAPTA relied on a restrictive positive list of rarely traded items, whereas SAFTA introduced a negative list to cover all unlisted goods.

quiz.q: According to the notes, which external and structural factor distinguished SAARC from successful blocs like ASEAN and the EU?
options: SAARC members possessed fully consolidated nationalisms that resisted any economic cooperation with neighbouring states.
SAARC lacked an external push factor like the United States that encouraged regional integration in other blocs.
SAARC faced continuous military interventions by external superpowers seeking direct colonial control over South Asian territory.
SAARC was hindered because economic considerations completely overwhelmed domestic political priorities across all member states.
quiz.why: According to the notes, the United States served as an external push factor for European and Southeast Asian integration, which SAARC lacked.

quiz.q: Why did India pursue the BBIN sub-regional platform, and what principal domestic obstacle hindered its full implementation?
options: Bangladesh opposed maritime border adjustments, prompting India to abandon trilateral connectivity plans with Bhutan and Nepal.
Nepal rejected transit rights over environmental concerns, delaying the formal ratification of the motor vehicle treaty.
Pakistan vetoed the regional motor agreement, while Bhutan's parliament withheld ratification citing local transport and environmental concerns.
Sri Lanka demanded maritime security pacts, causing India to restrict transport agreements exclusively to landlocked partners.
quiz.why: India initiated BBIN after Pakistan vetoed the regional motor agreement in 2014, but Bhutan delayed ratification due to domestic transport and ecological concerns.

quiz.q: Why does India prioritize BIMSTEC as a pragmatic diplomatic and economic alternative to SAARC?
options: BIMSTEC enforces a common defence pact that automatically excludes external powers from operating in the Indian Ocean.
BIMSTEC replaces consensus decision-making with majority voting, preventing smaller member nations from using national vetoes.
BIMSTEC restricts cooperation solely to counter-terrorism, avoiding contentious free trade agreements and regional economic integration.
It bypasses Pakistan's obstructionist veto while linking South Asia to high-growth Southeast Asian economies like Thailand.
quiz.why: BIMSTEC offers India a way to circumvent Pakistan's obstructionism within SAARC while building economic bridges to dynamic Southeast Asian partners like Thailand.
